title: Azure / App Service / Overview
description: Azure Monitor platform metrics for one App Service web app (microsoft.web/sites) and its App Service plan (microsoft.web/serverfarms), plus a Resource Graph inventory of all web apps in the subscription. Function apps on dedicated plans use the same microsoft.web/sites namespace. Fleet health across all apps (Azure Monitor Baseline Alerts KPIs from Log Analytics) is in the bundled 'Azure / Infrastructure / Apps Monitoring' dashboard (link at the top). Managed by Terraform (azure-managed-grafana, dashboards/app-service/app-service-overview.json): edit the file, not the dashboard in the UI; changes made in Grafana are overwritten on the next apply.

links.title: Azure portal
links.tooltip: Open the selected resource in the Azure portal

links.title: Diagnose and solve problems
links.tooltip: Azure's built-in diagnostics for the selected resource

links.title: Operations overview
links.tooltip: State, alerts and changes across all covered resources

panels.title: Troubleshooting - $resource
panels.description: Start here when something looks wrong: is the resource running, has an alert fired, what changed? Resource Graph data; it lags a few minutes behind Azure. Grafana's identity needs read access (Monitoring Reader) on the resource.

panels.title: State
panels.description: Current state from Azure Resource Manager. Green: running/ready. Red: stopped, deallocated, failed or disabled. Orange: anything else, e.g. updating or starting.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.Web/sites' and resourceGroup =~ '$rg' and name =~ '$resource'
| project ['State'] = tostring(properties.state), ['Availability'] = tostring(properties.availabilityState)

panels.title: Open alerts
panels.description: Azure Monitor alerts fired on this resource and not closed (alerts are kept 30 days). History across resources: the bundled Azure / Alert Consumption dashboard.

azureResourceGraph.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tolower(tostring(e.targetResource)) == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource')
| where tostring(e.monitorCondition) == 'Fired' and tostring(e.alertState) != 'Closed'
| summarize ['Open alerts'] = count()

panels.title: Changes (time range)
panels.description: Resource Manager changes to this resource and its child resources in the time range (Resource Graph change history, kept 14 days). Details on the right.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| summarize Changes = count()

panels.title: What changed
panels.description: Latest Resource Manager changes in the time range: who changed what, with which operation, and which properties. A change just before a problem started is the first suspect.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| project Time = todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp),
          Change = tostring(properties.changeType),
          Resource = iff(target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource'), '(this resource)', substring(target, strlen(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/$resource')) + 1)),
          ['Changed by'] = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.changedBy),
          Operation = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.operation),
          Properties = strcat_array(bag_keys(properties.changes), ', ')
| order by Time desc
| take 50

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Total requests (Requests, Total) to the selected web app over the time range, all status codes. Includes requests to the SCM (Kudu) site. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx
panels.description: Requests answered with 5xx (Http5xx, Total) over the time range. Only requests that reached the workers are counted; front-end failures are not. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: HTTP 4xx
panels.description: Requests answered with 4xx (Http4xx, Total) over the time range. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Avg response time
panels.description: Mean of HttpResponseTime (Average) over the time range. HttpResponseTime replaces the deprecated AverageResponseTime. Thresholds 1 s / 3 s are a starting point. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Health check status
panels.description: Last value of HealthCheckStatus (Average). 100 means every instance passes the health check path; lower values mean instances were deemed unhealthy. Empty when no Health check path is configured. The metric only supports PT5M/PT1H/P1D grains. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Plan CPU
panels.description: Last value of the App Service plan CpuPercentage (Average across instances). App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Plan memory
panels.description: Last value of the App Service plan MemoryPercentage (Average across instances). App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Plan HTTP queue
panels.description: Last value of the App Service plan HttpQueueLength (Average): requests waiting to be served. A growing queue means the plan is overloaded. App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Inventory - all web apps in the subscription
Web apps in subscription
panels.description: Azure Resource Graph inventory of every microsoft.web/sites resource in the selected subscription (web apps, and Function / Logic apps that share the namespace; Function apps on dedicated plans report the same metrics as web apps). 'runtime' comes from linuxFxVersion (Linux) or windowsFxVersion (Windows containers); it is empty for classic Windows stacks, whose runtime is not exposed in Resource Graph. Deployment slots (microsoft.web/sites/slots) are not listed. Click a name to load its metrics below (the plan is preselected only if it is in the same resource group). Fleet health across all apps: 'Azure / Infrastructure / Apps Monitoring'.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.web/sites'
| extend sp = properties.siteProperties.properties
| extend linuxFx = iff(tostring(sp[0].name) =~ 'LinuxFxVersion', tostring(sp[0].value), iff(tostring(sp[1].name) =~ 'LinuxFxVersion', tostring(sp[1].value), iff(tostring(sp[2].name) =~ 'LinuxFxVersion', tostring(sp[2].value), '')))
| extend windowsFx = iff(tostring(sp[0].name) =~ 'WindowsFxVersion', tostring(sp[0].value), iff(tostring(sp[1].name) =~ 'WindowsFxVersion', tostring(sp[1].value), iff(tostring(sp[2].name) =~ 'WindowsFxVersion', tostring(sp[2].value), '')))
| extend runtime = coalesce(tostring(properties.siteConfig.linuxFxVersion), linuxFx, tostring(properties.siteConfig.windowsFxVersion), windowsFx)
| extend farm = split(tostring(properties.serverFarmId), '/')
| project name, resourceGroup, location, kind, state = tostring(properties.state), plan = tostring(farm[8]), planResourceGroup = tostring(farm[4]), planSku = tostring(properties.sku), httpsOnly = tobool(properties.httpsOnly), runtime, defaultHostName = tostring(properties.defaultHostName)
| order by name asc

panels.title: HTTP - $resource
panels.description: Platform HTTP metrics of the selected web app. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Requests by instance
panels.description: Requests (Total) per time grain, split by the Instance dimension. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: HTTP status codes
panels.description: Http2xx, Http3xx, Http4xx and Http5xx (Total) per time grain, all instances. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Response time by instance
panels.description: HttpResponseTime (Average) split by Instance. Uses the current HttpResponseTime metric, not the deprecated AverageResponseTime. Dashed lines at 1 s / 3 s. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx by instance
panels.description: Http5xx (Total) per time grain, split by Instance. Anything above 0 deserves a look. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Health check status by instance
panels.description: HealthCheckStatus (Average) split by Instance; 100 = healthy. Only the PT5M/PT1H/P1D grains exist for this metric. Empty when no Health check path is configured. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: HTTP 4xx detail
panels.description: Http401, Http403, Http404 and Http406 (Total) per time grain, all instances. Compare with the Http4xx total in 'HTTP status codes'. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Data in / out
panels.description: BytesReceived (Data in) and BytesSent (Data out), Total bytes per time grain, all instances. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Process resources - $resource
panels.description: Per-app process counters of the selected web app. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: CPU time by instance
panels.description: CpuTime (Total): CPU seconds consumed by the app per time grain, split by Instance. Plan-level CPU percentage is in the App Service plan section. Not reported for Function apps.

panels.title: Memory working set by instance
panels.description: MemoryWorkingSet (Average) split by Instance. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: App Service plan - $plan
panels.description: Metrics of the App Service plan selected in the 'App Service plan' variable. App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Plan CPU percentage by instance
panels.description: CpuPercentage (Average) of the plan, split by Instance. Dashed line at 80 %. App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Plan memory percentage by instance
panels.description: MemoryPercentage (Average) of the plan, split by Instance. Dashed line at 80 %. App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Plan HTTP / disk queue length
panels.description: HttpQueueLength and DiskQueueLength (Average) of the plan, all instances. High HTTP queue = plan under heavy load; high disk queue = excessive disk I/O. App Service plan metrics exist only for Basic, Standard, Premium and Isolated tiers. Pick the plan with the 'App Service plan' variable (same resource group as $rg).

panels.title: Windows apps only - $resource
panels.description: Windows-only process counters (application queue, private bytes, connections, threads, handles). Linux web apps don't emit them and Azure Monitor rejects the queries, so this row is collapsed: it only queries when expanded.

panels.title: Requests in application queue by instance
panels.description: RequestsInApplicationQueue (Average) split by Instance. Also one of the Azure Monitor Baseline Alerts KPIs used by 'Azure / Infrastructure / Apps Monitoring'. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Private bytes by instance
panels.description: PrivateBytes (Average) split by Instance: memory the app process allocated that cannot be shared. Also an Azure Monitor Baseline Alerts KPI. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Connections by instance
panels.description: AppConnections (Average): bound sockets in the sandbox, split by Instance. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Threads by instance
panels.description: Threads (Average): active threads in the app process, split by Instance. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.

panels.title: Handles by instance
panels.description: Handles (Average): open handles of the app process, split by Instance. Function apps on dedicated (App Service / Premium) plans also emit these metrics under microsoft.web/sites, so they can be picked in the Web app variable too.
